title: Prefix Codes and Finite Lossless Coding

items.title: Finite discrete sources and product blocks
items.statement:
A **finite discrete source** is an integer $m\ge1$ and a probability vector $p=(p_1,\ldots,p_m)$ on the alphabet $\mathcal X=[m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}$ such that $p_i>0$ for every $i$. Here a probability vector has nonnegative entries summing to one, as in [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]]; the strict positivity convention means that $\mathcal X$ is the source support. In particular, the one-symbol source has $m=1$ and $p_1=1$.

For $n\ge1$, a **block of length $n$** is a word $x^n=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathcal X^n$. Its product probability is
$$p^n(x^n):=\prod_{t=1}^n p_{x_t}.$$
Finite distributivity gives $\sum_{x^n\in\mathcal X^n}p^n(x^n)=(\sum_{i=1}^m p_i)^n=1$, so $p^n$ is again a probability vector and has full support. Blocks are the only memoryless-source objects used on this page.

items.title: Base-two entropy of a finite source
items.statement:
For a finite source $p$ of [[def-finite-discrete-source-and-blocks]], define its **base-two Shannon entropy**, measured in bits, by
$$H_2(p):=\frac{H(p)}{\ln 2}=-\sum_{i=1}^m p_i\log_2 p_i.$$
Here $H(p)=-\sum_i p_i\ln p_i$ is the finite Shannon entropy in natural units from [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]]. The equality follows from $\log_2 t=\ln(t)/\ln 2$ and $\sum_i p_i=1$. Every $p_i$ is positive by the source convention, so no zero-term convention is needed here.

items.title: Finite binary source codes, extension, and expected length
items.statement:
A **binary word** is a finite sequence of symbols from $\{0,1\}$. The set $\{0,1\}^*$ includes the empty word $\varepsilon$, and $\{0,1\}^+$ is the set of nonempty binary words. A **binary source code** for the finite source $\mathcal X=[m]$ is a function $C:\mathcal X\to\{0,1\}^+$. Its codeword length is $\ell_i:=|C(i)|\ge1$.

The **extension** $C^*:\mathcal X^*\to\{0,1\}^*$ maps the empty source word to $\varepsilon$ and maps $i_1\cdots i_n$ to $C(i_1)\cdots C(i_n)$. The code is **uniquely decodable** if $C^*$ is injective, including comparisons between source words of different lengths. Its expected length for source law $p$ is
$$L_p(C):=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i\ell_i.$$

items.title: Binary prefix codes and their code trees
items.statement:
A binary code $C$ is a **prefix code** if it is nonsingular and no codeword $C(i)$ is a proper prefix of a different codeword $C(j)$. A word $u$ is a proper prefix of $v$ when $v=uw$ for some nonempty binary word $w$. Nonsingular means $C(i)\ne C(j)$ whenever $i\ne j$.

The **code tree** is the finite rooted trie whose vertices are all prefixes of codewords, whose root is $\varepsilon$, and whose edges append one bit, labeled $0$ or $1$. Since the code is prefix-free, its codewords are exactly the leaves; unused branches are absent. A binary word path from the root records its successive edge labels.

items.title: McMillan inequality for finite binary uniquely decodable codes
items.statement:
Let $C$ be a finite binary uniquely decodable code with lengths $\ell_i$. Then
$$\sum_{i=1}^m2^{-\ell_i}\le1.$$

items.title: Ideal-real arithmetic interval coding for a fixed block
items.statement:
Fix a finite full-support source $p=(p_1,\ldots,p_m)$, its symbol order $1<\cdots<m$, and a public block length $n\ge1$. The **ideal-real arithmetic interval** of the empty prefix is $[0,1)$. If a prefix has interval $[a,b)$ and the next symbol is $i$, assign the extended prefix the half-open subinterval
$$\left[a+(b-a)\sum_{j<i}p_j,\ a+(b-a)\sum_{j\le i}p_j\right).$$
This subdivision is performed exactly over the real numbers.

For a completed block $x^n$, let $I(x^n)=[a,b)$ be its resulting interval, put $w=b-a$, and define
$$r=\left\lfloor-\log_2w\right\rfloor,\qquad s=r+2,\qquad k=\left\lfloor2^s\frac{a+b}{2}\right\rfloor.$$
The ideal-real codeword is the $s$-bit binary representation of $k$, with leading zeros. Each encoding frame contains exactly one length-$n$ source block; the decoder knows $p$ and $n$. A stream uses an externally known number of such frames. No finite-register or finite-precision implementation is specified by this definition.

items.title: Binary Kraft criterion for finite positive codeword lengths
items.statement:
For a finite list of positive integers $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_m$, there is a binary prefix code on $[m]$ having codeword lengths $\ell_i$ if and only if
$$\sum_{i=1}^m2^{-\ell_i}\le1.$$

items.title: Deterministic binary Huffman coding
items.statement:
**Input:** A finite full-support source $(m,p)$ as in [[def-finite-discrete-source-and-blocks]], with the symbols ordered $1,\ldots,m$.

**Output:** A binary prefix code $C_H$ on these symbols.

If $m=1$, return the one-bit codeword $C_H(1)=0$.

If $m\ge2$, make one active leaf for each source symbol $i$, with weight $p_i$ and serial number $i$. Repeatedly do the following while more than one node is active:

1. Order active nodes lexicographically by (weight, serial number), using the ordinary order on real weights and then integer serials.
2. Remove the first two nodes. Make a new parent whose left child is the first removed node and whose right child is the second, whose weight is their sum, and whose serial is the next unused integer.
3. Insert this parent among the active nodes.

When one root remains, label every left edge $0$ and every right edge $1$. The codeword for symbol $i$ is the edge-label sequence on the path from the root to its original leaf. The order by serial number fixes all ties and fixes the bit orientation. The same merge rule applies to any finite active list of positive weights carrying distinct serial numbers; the source input initializes the serials as $1,\ldots,m$, and each new parent receives a fresh serial.

For each $m\ge2$, the algorithm executes exactly $m-1$ merges because each merge decreases the number of active nodes by one. The returned tree is finite. The next theorem proves the code is prefix-free and optimal; no complexity bound is asserted.

items.title: Ideal-real interval coding is prefix-free and lossless
items.statement: For fixed $p$ and $n$, the code in [[def-ideal-real-arithmetic-interval-code]] is injective and prefix-free on $\mathcal X^n$. Its codeword length for $x^n$ is at most $-\log_2p^n(x^n)+2$. Thus an $n$-block is recovered uniquely, and concatenated frames of this fixed block length are uniquely parsed.

items.title: Exact finite-register arithmetic coding for rational block sources
items.statement:
**Configuration and frame model.** The shared model consists of positive integers $q_1,\ldots,q_m$, their total $Q=\sum_iq_i$, and the rational source $p_i=q_i/Q$. Fix a maximum frame length $N\ge1$ and a frame length $n$ with $1\le n\le N$. Every frame is exactly one $n$-symbol block; the decoder knows $q_1,\ldots,q_m,Q,N,n$. A complete stream contains a specified finite number $R$ of such frames, supplied by an outer frame count. The arithmetic coder adds no end marker.

**Register size.** Let $B$ be the least integer $b\ge0$ such that $Q^N\le2^b$. Endpoint and width registers have $B+1$ bits; the output index has at most $B+2$ bits; the largest temporary numerator below is stored in $2B+4$ bits. Counters store the finite ranges $0,\ldots,N$ and $0,\ldots,B+2$. All arithmetic is exact integer addition, multiplication, comparison, and floor division; no floating-point rounding or register growth during a frame is allowed.

**Encoder.** Put $c_i=\sum_{j<i}q_j$ and $D=Q^n$. For an input block $x^n=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$, initialize $L=0$ and $W=1$. For $t=1,\ldots,n$, set $r=n-t$ and update
$$L\leftarrow L+Wc_{x_t}Q^r,\qquad W\leftarrow Wq_{x_t}.$$
After the $n$ updates, search the finite list $j=0,\ldots,B$ and retain the largest $u$ satisfying $2^uW\le D$. Set $s=u+2$ and
$$k=\left\lfloor\frac{2^s(2L+W)}{2D}\right\rfloor.$$
Emit the $s$-bit binary representation of $k$, padded on the left with zeros.

**Decoder.** For fixed $n$, generate the finite codebook by applying the encoder to every block in $[m]^n$ and build its binary trie. For one frame, read payload bits along this trie until a leaf is reached and return its block; reject an invalid path or a path not reaching a leaf within $B+2$ bits. For a stream, repeat this operation exactly $R$ times and then stop. The next theorem proves that the generated codebook is prefix-free and that every encoded frame reaches exactly one leaf.

The configured register widths are finite for each fixed rational model and cap $N$. They grow when a new configuration with a larger $N$ or $Q$ is installed; no constant-word-width streaming guarantee is claimed.

items.title: Shannon bounds for finite binary codes
items.statement:
Let $p$ be a finite full-support source and let $H_2(p)$ be its entropy in bits. Every finite binary uniquely decodable code $C$ satisfies $L_p(C)\ge H_2(p)$. If $m\ge2$, there is a binary prefix code with lengths
$$\ell_i=\left\lceil-\log_2p_i\right\rceil$$
and expected length strictly less than $H_2(p)+1$. If $m=1$, the one-bit codeword $0$ has length $1=H_2(p)+1$.

items.title: The deterministic Huffman code is prefix-optimal
items.statement: For every finite full-support source, the algorithm [[alg-binary-huffman-coding]] terminates, returns a binary prefix code, and minimizes $L_p(C)$ among all binary prefix codes on the same alphabet. For a one-symbol source it returns the one-bit codeword $0$, which is optimal among codes with nonempty codewords.

items.title: Huffman expected length is within one bit of entropy
items.statement:
Let $C_H$ be the code returned by [[alg-binary-huffman-coding]] for a finite full-support source $p$. If $m\ge2$, then
$$H_2(p)\le L_p(C_H)<H_2(p)+1.$$
If $m=1$, then $H_2(p)=0$ and $L_p(C_H)=1$.
